draft.title: Legal and ethical investing
card: Investors must follow the law. Insider trading, which means buying or selling shares using secret information the public does not have, is illegal in Australia.
Many investors also choose ethical investments. These avoid businesses or products the investor thinks cause harm, such as tobacco or fossil fuels.
Some managed funds are built this way. A fund can leave out certain industries, so investors can follow their values without picking each share themselves.

Being legal and being ethical are different tests. An investment can be legal but still go against an investor's values. Ethical funds may also earn less or more than other funds, and the return is not guaranteed.
draft.remember: Legal investing follows the law. Ethical investing also follows the investor's values.

a.q: Sam picks a managed fund that leaves out tobacco companies because he thinks they cause harm. What type of investing is this?
opts: Ethical investing
Insider trading
Diversification
Investing with no risk
a.why: Sam is choosing a fund that avoids a harm he cares about, so it is ethical investing. It is not insider trading, which means using secret information and is illegal.
a.clue: He is choosing based on his values.

b.q: Priya invests in a coal mining company, which is legal. She later decides it goes against her values about climate change. What does this show?
opts: An investment can be legal but not ethical to her
An investment that is legal must also be ethical
Ethical investments are the only legal investments
She broke the law by investing in coal
b.why: Legal and ethical are different tests. The law allowed her investment, but her own values lead her to judge it differently. It is wrong to say legal means ethical, because ethics depend on the investor's values.
b.clue: Think about what the law covers and what values cover.

b.best: An investment can be legal but not ethical to her

problems.detail: The right option is the only hedged one ('can'), while the three wrong options use absolutes ('only', 'must', 'broke the law'). A test-wise student could pick it without knowing the idea.
